$comment: The frozen feature list. Coverage is measured against this, never against an agent's self-report. When the skill grows a feature it is added here, and the round that first sees it says so. Detection `not_instrumented` means we have no objective signal for it: it is listed and reported separately, never counted as used or unused, because a feature we cannot measure must not quietly depress the score. v3 (2026-08-29, after round 01): boundary.py is detected by the per-claim fields it actually writes, not a top-level key it never wrote; and three features added for the shape of the delivered artefact. Those three are measured here, by mechanical detection against this frozen list, and deliberately NOT by any scored rubric criterion: the skill gained them before this file named them, so a criterion written for them now would be the rubric chasing the skill.

features.note: Capture a source so a claim can still be checked after it moves
Append each claim as it is made
Log what was decided and rejected
Open a conflict when two sources disagree
Where a claim holds and where it fails, written as fields on the claim. Round 01 looked for a top-level `boundaries` key that no version writes.
Refuse a delivery that hides a disagreement
The dimensions the boundaries use are defined in the sidecar, so a boundary travels
One claim at several depths
What species of sentence a claim is
Derive claim status rather than store it

features.detect: artefact_re:^#{1,3}\s+.*(what is actually being claimed|what is being claimed|the claim, decomposed|reading of the claim)
features.note: The question was split into separately testable propositions and the split is in the artefact
The decomposition is rendered as a table a reader can take in at a glance
The verdict cell contains one of the five closed words and nothing else, so two papers can be read side by side
Each defined term says what it means in this paper, rather than instructing the reader
The propositions are enumerated and labelled P1..Pn, not merely counted
The verdict table is keyed to the propositions and its third column is headed Conditions

features.detect: artefact_re:^#{1,3}\s+.*(where this is going|where it is going|the forward view)
features.note: A forward-view section exists and is named, even if it says no forward view is supportable
Definitions are split into terms not used and terms used, so a block never mixes the two
Each defined term names its family, so the reader learns one diagnosis rather than six shapes
The verdict table restates the proposition beside its label, so a reader need not scroll back

A claim with no boundary says Unconditional in the Conditions column. This measures the generator, not the author: boundary.py emits it, so a miss means the table was written by hand or the generator was overridden.
Propositions are carried in the sidecar as claims, not only as prose in the artefact
At least one source contributes more than one quote, so a paper is not limited to one sentence per source
A quote that is not prose carries a plain-English gloss saying what the fragment means
A cited capture has an independent third-party copy, so custody is not entirely self-attested
A claim points at where it appears in the artefact, so the sidecar audits the paper and not only the ledger
Each claim records what was actually done to it, rather than who signed for it
An untested claim names the study or measurement that would settle it, so an absence is a route forward rather than a dead end
